summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following a left knee debridement and cement spacer replacement complicated by unexpected 1200 mL blood loss, leading to acute blood loss anemia. She was initially intubated and transfused multiple units of packed red blood cells due to a difficult crossmatch. Cultures confirmed MSSA and Group B Streptococcus joint infection, prompting a switch to IV cefazolin. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. She developed antibiotic-associated diarrhea, managed with loperamide and diphenoxylate-atropine, and a concurrent E. coli UTI treated by cefazolin. Warfarin was initiated for DVT prophylaxis with close INR monitoring due to tacrolimus interaction. Her kidney function and acidosis improved, and she was discharged home with home health services for six weeks of IV antibiotics, follow-up labs, and wound care instructions.
